newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fortis sees GAN buy opportunity - co-chairman.
newsitem.headline: Fortis sees GAN buy opportunity - co-chairman.

text.p: Maurice Lippens, co-chairman of Belgo-Dutch bancassurance group Fortis, said on Wednesday that the group was actively looking at a number of acquisitions.

Fortis was interested in buying a stake in French insurer GAN. "GAN is one opportunity among others...which we are very actively looking at," he told journalists after the Fortis AG annual shareholders meeting.
"There is no formal commitment to look at GAN yet, but it is something we cannot afford not to look at."
Lippens said the increase in banking and insurance mergers ahead of the arrival of the euro had made the group more proactive in looking for new opportunities.

In his speech to shareholders he noted the merger of Banque Paribas Belgium and Bacob Bank and rumours that rival Belgian insurer Royale Belge, along with its stake in bank BBL, could be sold to Dutch financial services group ING.

"If Royale Belge and BBL went to ING it would mean we would have a very strong player against us," he told journalists. "It probably would not change the situation on the Benelux market dramatically today or tomorrow, but maybe in a few years. We would have to see then what we could do about it."
Lippens said he did not know if Royale Belge parent AXA -UAP had decided to sell the company or its other AXA Belgium unit.
He did not expect Royale Belge to make any announcement at today's annual shareholders meeting.

However, AXA-UAP chairman Claude Bebear appeared to have interests in other parts of the world, notably Asia, and a Royale Belge or AXA Belgium sale could be feasible if AXA-UAP wanted to make a new acquisition or reduce debt, he said.
